title: Hybrid anticipatory prefetch scheduler for heterogeneous multi-GPU kernel routing
creator: Ava Ramirez
description:
Problem: We see persistent tail latency and NCCL congestion spikes during mixed prefill/decode workloads on heterogeneous clusters. The runtime often chooses suboptimal kernels for incoming prefill batches because it lacks lookahead about sequence-length distribution and in-flight communication windows. This results in stalled kernels, bursty NCCL traffic, and lower GPU utilization.

Goal: Implement a hybrid anticipatory prefetch scheduler that (1) predicts per-request prefill/decode characteristics, (2) reserves short communication windows to increase NCCL overlap with compute, and (3) surfaces per-device kernel hints so the kernel selector can prefer attention implementations that minimize comm-bound stalls. Targets: reduce 99th percentile latency for short interactive requests by 20%, improve token throughput for mixed workloads by 10%, and reduce NCCL bandwidth queuing events by 30% on heterogeneous clusters.
design_notes:
High-level components: prediction service (EWMA + lightweight classifier per route), lookahead timeline builder (30-100ms window), per-device slot allocator, NCCL overlap orchestrator, and kernel-hint API between scheduler and kernel selector.

Algorithm: 1) On request enqueue, prediction produces an expected 'phase' vector: {prefill-len, decode-len, preferred-seq-range}. 2) Timeline builder aggregates predictions within a short aggregation window (configurable, default 8ms) to produce microbatches and assign NCCL overlap slots to ranks that will perform bulky collective ops. 3) Slot allocator attempts to align compute work so that heavy NCCL ops execute while adjacent ranks are busy with local compute, maximizing overlap. 4) Kernel-hint API exposes 'comm-friendly' vs 'compute-dense' suggestions; kernel selector uses a fast cost heuristic to prefer kernels that reduce cross-device communication when overlap is likely.

Edge cases & fallbacks: if prediction confidence is low, fall back to existing round-robin token router. For highly skewed workloads (all long sequences), scheduler disables overlap windows to avoid wasted reservations.

Instrumentation: add counters for predicted vs actual sequence length, NCCL overlap success ratio, per-kernel stall time, and scheduler overhead CPU cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Canary end-to-end tests show >=15% reduction in p99 for interactive short sequences on heterogeneous cluster A
Integration perf tests demonstrate >=8% token/s throughput improvement for mixed-short/long synthetic workload
NCCL queueing metric reduced by >=20% in stress runs
Scheduler CPU overhead stays under 3% of serving cpu budget at 5k RPS
rollout_plan: 1) Unit & integration tests in CI. 2) Deploy to internal staging clusters with instrumentation enabled. 3) Canary on dedicated cluster runtime-canary-03 with 5% of PLG traffic for 48h. 4) Monitor p99/p50 latency, GPU occupancy, NCCL queue metrics, and revert if p99 regressions >5% or NCCL queuing increases. 5) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with automated health gates. Backout path: toggles in scheduler config to disable lookahead allocation and kernel hints.
